card.name: Drug-interaction text before enzyme or transporter terms
card.fires_on: Linking words (is, that, are, for) and the end of drug names in drug-interaction sections, right before the text names an enzyme or transporter (CYP3A4, UGT, BCRP, P-gp) or a drug effect on levels.

modes.label: Linking word after a drug
modes.description: A small word such as is, that, which or are after a drug name or the word drugs, leading into a metabolism or substrate statement.
modes.example: Coadministration of ISENTRESS or ISENTRESS HD with drugs that<< are>> strong inducers of UGT1A

modes.label: Inside a drug name
modes.description: The last piece of a drug name such as fluconazole or rosuvastatin, before the effect on another drug is described.
modes.example: There was a significant increase in zidovudine AUC following the administration of flu<<con>>azole.

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words like drug, pharmac and plasma, so the next words talk about drugs and their levels.
card.plain: It marks the spot in a drug-interaction passage where the text is about to say how one drug affects another.
